judged_text: The multi-host destination-calendar collection is gated on eventType.schedulingType === 'COLLECTIVE', excluding dynamic group bookings even though the removed comment explicitly named 'dynamic collective events' as needing per-member destinationCalendar handling. Dynamic multi-user bookings still create the calendar event only on the organizer's destination calendar, so the other invited users' calendars never see the booking — the exact gap this PR claims to close.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking`, additional users’ destination calendars are collected specifically when `eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE"` (and `isTeamEventType` is true) and then appended via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);`. Since `isTeamEventType` is derived from `eventType.schedulingType` being in `["COLLECTIVE","ROUND_ROBIN"]`, “dynamic collective” events (i.e., those with `schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE"`) are not excluded by this gate—they are exactly what the code targets. The diff also updates calendar creation to iterate `event.destinationCalendar` (array) and create events per destination in `createAllCalendarEvents`, so the claim that multi-host calendars “never see the booking” is not supported for COLLECTIVE. The finding’s assertion about excluded “dynamic collective events” misreads the implemented condition and behavior shown in the diff.
